source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

32003.t:
In the governor's race, Democrat Aaron Ford beat Republican Joe Lombardo in Clark County by about 16 points, 412,966 votes to 297,961. Kamala Harris carried it by about 3 points in 2024, so the county moved 13 points toward the Democrats. That was the largest shift of Nevada's 17 counties, well above the typical county's 6 points and a bit above the statewide 11. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points.

Turnout fell sharply. The 741,428 votes cast were 72% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Nearby, Washoe moved 8 points left, Carson City 5 points left, and Douglas 3 points right.

32510.t:
Carson City stayed Republican in the race for Nevada governor but by less than in 2024. Lombardo beat Ford here 12,656 to 11,034, a margin of 7 points, after Trump carried the county by 11. That is a 5-point move toward the Democrats, smaller than the state's 11-point shift and the typical Nevada county's 6. It ranks 11th of 17 counties by move. Neighboring Washoe moved 8 points left and Clark 13, while Douglas moved 3 points right.

About 24,937 votes were cast, 80% of the 2024 total. With that drop, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

32031.t:
In the race for Nevada governor, Washoe County went from a narrow Democratic edge for Harris in 2024, about 1 point, to a 9-point win for Ford over Lombardo, 106,895 votes to 89,282. That 8-point shift toward the Democrats ranks sixth among Nevada's 17 counties and beats the typical Nevada county's 6 points, though it trails the state's 11-point swing, Clark County's 13 and the national typical move of 14.

Turnout was 205,200, or 78% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Washoe cast the state's second-most votes, behind only Clark.

32021.t:
In the race for Nevada governor, Mineral County backed Republican Lombardo over Democrat Ford 1,001 to 558, a margin of 26 points. In 2024 Trump carried it by 36, so the county moved 10 points toward the Democrats. That was a bigger shift than the typical Nevada county's 6 points, ranking fourth of 17, though smaller than the state's 11-point swing and the national county median of 14.

Turnout fell sharply: 1,708 votes, 74% of the 2024 total. The count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Similar Republican counties moved less. Storey shifted 3 points left, Nye 6, and Douglas moved 3 points right.

32029.t:
In the governor's race, Storey County stayed firmly Republican but moved about 4 points toward the Democrats. Lombardo won it 1,578 to 720 over Ford, a margin of 35 points, down from Trump's 39-point margin in 2024. That shift was smaller than the typical Nevada county's 6-point move, ranking 13th of 17. It was also smaller than similar counties nearby: Lyon moved 7 points, Nye 6 and Mineral 10. The state as a whole swung 11 points to elect Ford.

Turnout fell to 2,443 votes, 79% of the 2024 total. The count therefore cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

32009.t:
In the governor's race, Esmeralda County voted for Lombardo over Ford by 289 votes to 71, a Republican margin of 56 points. That is 10 points less Republican than its 66-point margin for Trump in 2024. Ford won Nevada by 8 points, a statewide swing of 11 toward the Democrats. Esmeralda's shift ranks third among Nevada's 17 counties, ahead of the typical county's 6 points but short of the national county typical of 14. Similar rural counties moved less: Lander 7 points left, Lincoln barely at all, and Eureka 1 point right.

Esmeralda cast the fewest votes in the state, 391, only 85% of its 2024 turnout. With that drop, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

32019.t: In the governor's race, Lyon County stayed firmly Republican: Lombardo beat Ford 15,860 to 6,796, a margin of 38 points. That is 7 points narrower than Trump's 44-point win over Harris here in 2024, a shift toward the Democrats close to the typical Nevada county's 6 points but smaller than the state's 11-point swing and about half the typical national move of 14. Neighbors moved less: Nye 6 points, Churchill 4, and Douglas 3 toward Republicans. Only 24,096 votes were cast, 72% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

32011.t:
Eureka County barely moved in Nevada's race for governor, which Ford, the Democrat, won statewide by 8 points over Lombardo. The Republican carried the county 665 to 61, a margin of 78 points, against Trump's 78-point margin in 2024. That is a shift of about 1 point toward the Republicans, while the state moved 11 points toward the Democrats and the typical Nevada county moved 6. Eureka ranks 16th of 17 counties by move. Lincoln, a similarly lopsided county, was also nearly flat, while Esmeralda and Lander moved 10 and 7 points left.

Only 770 votes were cast, 74% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate changed minds from voters who stayed home. With just under 95% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

32033.t:
In the race for Nevada governor, White Pine County stayed firmly Republican, backing Lombardo over Ford 2,205 to 635, a margin of R+51. That is 6 points less Republican than Trump's R+57 margin over Harris in 2024, matching the typical move among Nevada's 17 counties and well short of the state's 11-point swing as Ford won statewide by 8. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

Only 3,068 votes were cast, 71% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Similar counties moved by varying amounts: Pershing by 3 points, Humboldt by 8 and Elko by 11.

32015.t:
In the governor's race, Lombardo carried Lander County 1,469 to 372 over Ford, a Republican margin of 55 points. Trump won it by 62 in 2024, so the county moved 7 points toward the Democrats. That ranks seventh of Nevada's 17 counties. The typical county in the state moved 6, and Nevada as a whole moved 11 as Ford won statewide by 8. Nationally the typical county moved 14.

Turnout was 1,996 votes, 73% of the 2,725 cast in 2024. With that drop, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar Nevada counties, White Pine moved 6 points, Pershing 3 and Esmeralda 10.

32023.t:
Nye County stayed firmly Republican in the race for governor, but by a smaller margin than in 2024. Lombardo beat Ford 13,583 to 5,894, a margin of about 37 points, down from Trump's 42-point win here. That is a 5-point move toward the Democrats, close to the typical Nevada county's 6 points but well short of the statewide 11-point swing that carried Ford to an 8-point win, and far below the national typical move of 14.

Turnout fell sharply, to 20,902 votes, 77% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among similar counties, Lyon moved 7 points left and Churchill 4, while Douglas moved 3 points toward the Republicans.

32005.t:
In the governor's race, Douglas County went against the state's direction. Lombardo, the Republican, carried it 19,105 to 8,825 over Ford, a margin of 36 points. That is 3 points wider than Trump's 33-point edge over Harris in 2024. Statewide, Ford won by 8 points, a shift of 11 points toward the Democrats. Douglas was one of only two Nevada counties to move right, and it moved furthest right of all 17. Similar counties moved left: Nye by 6 points, Lyon by 7 and Mineral by 9.

About 28,945 votes were cast, 81% of the 2024 total. With that drop, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

32017.t:
Lincoln County barely moved in Nevada's race for governor, where Ford beat Lombardo statewide by about 8 points. Lombardo carried the county 1,607 to 205, a margin of 72 points, against Trump's 73-point win over Harris in 2024. That is a shift of less than a point toward the Democrats. Turnout was 79% of the 2024 vote, 1,943 ballots against 2,472, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

The state as a whole moved about 11 points left, and the typical Nevada county moved 6. Lincoln ranks 15th of 17. Among similar small, heavily Republican counties, Eureka moved a point right, while Lander moved 7 points left and Esmeralda 10. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

32007.t:
In the race for Nevada governor, Elko County stayed firmly Republican but moved about 11 points toward the Democrats. Joe Lombardo beat Aaron Ford here 10,463 to 3,538, a margin of 46 points, down from Trump's 57-point margin in 2024. That swing matched the statewide shift of 11 points, which Ford rode to victory, and was the second-largest of Nevada's 17 counties, where the typical move was 6 points. Similar counties moved less: Humboldt 8, White Pine 6 and Churchill 4. Nationally the typical county moved 14 points.

Only 15,022 votes were cast, about two-thirds of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

32001.t:
Churchill County stayed solidly Republican in the race for Nevada governor, giving Lombardo 6,745 votes to Ford's 2,267, a margin of 46 points. That is 4 points closer than Trump's 50-point win over Harris in 2024, a smaller shift than in most of Nevada, where the typical county moved 6 points toward the Democrats and the state as a whole moved 11. Comparable counties shifted more: Humboldt 8 points, Lyon 7 and Elko 11.

Only 9,642 votes were cast, 71% of the 2024 total. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell whether people changed their minds or some simply stayed home.

32013.t:
Humboldt County stayed firmly Republican in the governor's race but moved toward the Democrats. Joe Lombardo led Aaron Ford 3,895 to 1,268, a 48-point margin, down from Donald Trump's 55-point margin over Kamala Harris in 2024. That is a shift of just under 8 points, fifth-largest among Nevada's 17 counties. It exceeds the typical Nevada county's 6 points but trails the state's 11-point swing and the national county median of 14. Among similarly Republican counties, Elko moved 11 points, White Pine 6 and Pershing 3.

Only 5,533 votes were cast, 69% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With 90% of the expected vote counted, these numbers may still move.

32027.t:
In Nevada's governor's race, Lombardo carried Pershing County 1,229 to 343 over Ford, a Republican margin of about 52 points. That is down from Trump's roughly 55-point win in 2024, a shift of between 2 and 3 points toward the Democrats. It was among the smallest moves in the state, 14th of 17 counties, against a typical Nevada county's 6 points and a national typical move of 14. Similar rural counties moved more: White Pine 6 points, Lander 7 and Humboldt 8.

Turnout fell sharply, with 1,689 votes cast against 2,308 in 2024. The count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.
